capabilities: Build flows from Dataview queries, folders, tags, properties, or bookmark groups
Sync edits within a flow back to the correct source notes
Rebuild flows automatically when source notes change
Navigate flows via file explorer, fuzzy modal, and flow switcher
Export flows as clean notes with UUIDs stripped
disambiguation: Not a text formatter or processor; it composes multiple source notes into one editable document and syncs edits back to them.
extras: Not yet on the community marketplace; install via BRAT or manually. The README warns users may find bugs, recommends running Obsidian's file recovery or another backup service, and includes an extensive troubleshooting guide and cheat sheet. Accepts tips on Ko-fi.
motivation: The author wanted to work on differently composed excerpts of the vault without manual copy-pasting and without the ordering and snapshot limits of the Outline core plugin.
problem: Obsidian offers no built-in Scrivenings-style way to view and edit many notes in one continuous document while keeping changes synced back to each source note.

relations.evidence: The Dataview plugin needs to be installed in order for textFlow to work.
If you want to use Flows with embeds, you'll have to install Sync Embeds by uthvah.

summary: Compiles multiple notes into a single editable flow and syncs edits back to the source notes, with flows defined from Dataview queries, folders, tags, properties, or bookmarks.
